description:
docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md Part B item B1.

=== DONE (s470bm) ===

SHIPPED
  tools/ir-inventory.pl        the generator
  docs/ir-op-inventory.tsv     682 rows, one per :pcl export (machine form)
  docs/ir-op-inventory.md      the same, grouped by family, §10 rule quoted
  Pl/t/ir-inventory-01.t       25 rows, 280 ms — the #1072 regenerate-and-
                               compare pattern plus shape assertions
  docs/ir-spec.md §10a         the `Contract:` grammar, normative
  cl/pcl-runtime.lisp          `Contract:` tails on 55 ops (docstring TEXT
                               only; 41 sites by script + 3 definer macros)

NUMBERS
  682 exported names; 53 families (19 are ir-spec §10 rows, 34 are families
  §10 has no row for); 0 UNCLASSIFIED; 55 ops carry a `Contract:` tail
  (numeric, numeric-compare, string, string-compare, elements).

THE DESIGN DECISION THAT MATTERS: the generator reads the LOADED runtime
(`do-external-symbols` in an SBCL with cl/pcl-runtime.lisp in it), not the
source text.  `p-+`, `p-*`, the six numeric compares, the six string compares
and the compound-assignment family have NO textual `(defun` anywhere — they
are expansions of `%def-overloaded-arith` / `%def-overloaded-cmp` /
`%def-overloaded-str-cmp`.  A text scan silently misses 20+ of the most-used
ops in the IR.  Cost: one SBCL start on the cached core.

THE CONTRACT GRAMMAR (ir-spec §10a): a final docstring paragraph
`Contract: ctx= coerce= magic= dies= dynamic= phase= host=`, seven keys with
CLOSED value sets; an unknown key or value DIES, and so does a PARTIAL tail
(absent must never read as a default).  The tail states the op's PERL
contract: where the implementation diverges, that is a bug (#1173), not a
weaker contract.

FINDINGS THE INVENTORY ITSELF PRODUCED
  * 16 names ir-spec §10 CITES do not exist: `p-&` `p-|` `p-^` `p-~` `p-x`
    `p-eq`..`p-cmp` `p-++` `p----` `p-++-post` `p----post` — Perl-facing
    spellings, not runtime names.  2 more exist but are INTERNAL:
    `%p-empty-list` (a runtime helper, never emitted) and `p-qr` (emitted
    package-QUALIFIED).  The tool classifies the two cases apart.
  * `p-||` and `p-` are the SAME symbol: `||` is an empty multiple-escape
    section, so the symbol's name is "P-" (probed).  A text-parsing backend
    must fold them — ir-spec §11b states the rule.
  * 27 exports have no definition: 25 TAP names (MEASURED from
    cl/pcl-test.lisp, never listed) plus `%_args` (a lambda-list name) and
    `p-backslash-list` (a place marker `p-setf`'s expansion matches on).
    Anything else undefined DIES naming itself (rule 12).

CAMPAIGN LEFT: 627 ops still print UNCLASSIFIED in the contract columns.  The
generator counts it per run, so the number is the progress bar.

=== MERGE-REVIEW CLOSE (s470bm) ===
Fable: "the spec must name real symbols — that is the whole point of B1."
§10's four wrong rows were CORRECTED, not merely annotated, in the style BK
used for `p-not` (the real symbols + one clause saying why the spelling
differs from perl's operator), each verified EMITTED first:

  bitwise         p-& p-| p-^ p-~   ->  p-bit-and p-bit-or p-bit-xor p-bit-not
  string ops      p-x               ->  p-str-x  (+ p-list-x named as the
                                        list-repetition twin; the two missing
                                        members p-string-concat and p-rindex
                                        added in the same pass)
  string compare  p-eq p-ne p-lt p-gt p-le p-ge p-cmp
                                    ->  p-str-eq … p-str-cmp
  increment       p-++ p---- p-++-post p----post
                                    ->  p-pre++ p-pre-- p-post++ p-post--

The two INTERNAL citations too: the regex row cited `(%p-empty-list)` as the
SPELLING of the empty list, which is never emitted (measured over 111 + 592
files) — the row now describes the VALUE (a zero-length vector) and marks the
helper runtime-internal.  `pcl::p-qr` §10 already spelled qualified; it is the
one citation still outstanding, because the symbol really is unexported —
#1177 owns it.

The tool's @SPEC10_CITED is the standing drift check and now reads
**18 stale → 1**; the generated .md header states that §10 was reconciled
against it, so a future reader knows the two were made to agree once.
subject: B1: the IR op inventory as GENERATED data (docs/ir-op-inventory.tsv/.md) + a regenerate-and-compare gate row + the `Contract:` docstring grammar, seeded on 55 ops
